Hmmm...this is a very interesting, and a surprisingly personal question. Well anyway these have changed my life:

Brave New World by Aldous Huxley, which is thoughtful sci-fi like I, Robot, and is eerily accurate in describing modern consumer culture like 80 years ahead of time. Almost every time I buy a coffee I think of soma, and almost every time I shop for clothes online, I think of Ending is better than mending.

The Double by Fyodor Dostoevsky. This one is really personal. Having had some issues with too much jealousy/competition/anger with other people, this book showed me that I actually had a fear of being replaced, of being useless. It's not a commonly liked book, but it hit home for me.

Gravity's Rainbow by Thomas Pynchon is just something else. The feelings that you get when reading that book, it's like shattering in slow motion. You can feel everything disintegrating in your hands. It's really weird, and I've never felt that way with any other book. Highly recommend it.

Fooled by Randomness by Nassim Taleb talks about how people can be over-confident, or over-explain things. Great read, and I've never been able to look at the news in the same way again.

House of Leaves by Mark Danielewski is scary af.
